text:
kevin: Quick follow-up on the RFC we merged last week — thinking about unifying the policy evaluation surface so the matchmaker and decider share a single minimal contract. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and surface migration checklist here.

elana: +1. can you bullet the main goals again?

kevin: Goals: 1) avoid duplicate scoring logic, 2) make runtime cheaper for small requests, 3) keep the policy DSL backward compatible, 4) enable better observability on decision provenance.

aj: Main risk is coupling runtime to policy expr semantics. if the runtime has to evaluate complex DSL, we lose deterministic perf.

sarah: Could we split responsibilities: matchmaker does coarse-grain scoring (cost/region/availability) and decider does fine-grain scoring (latency-per-tenant, affinity)? That keeps matchmaker light.

kevin: Yes — that was the initial idea. The RFC proposed a "score token" abstraction we could move between components. But some teams want both matchmaker and decider to be able to run the same rule sets for consistency.

elana: Tradeoff: duplication vs latency. If we centralize scoring in decider, matchmaker needs to wait on decider RPCs or cache results which adds complexity.

aj: Caching at matchmaker still possible: precompute coarse scores per region/instance type and TTL them. That avoids per-request RPCs.

sarah: Implementation thought: introduce compact preflight scores for matchmaker: {region, tier_score, cost_est, cold_bias}. Keep these cheap to compute. Decider receives full context and can re-score when tie-breaking.

kevin: Agree. Also need to decide where to evaluate tenant overrides and emergency SLAs. If matchmaker applies overrides, we get fast routing but duplication. If decider applies them, we have single source of truth but higher tail latency.

elana: My vote: preserve single source of truth for authoritative overrides (decider), but allow matchmaker to apply a best-effort shadow override for fast fast-path. Shadow outcomes must be telemetry-only and never be used without decider confirmation.

aj: That implies a new telemetry schema: preflight_decision and final_decision with provenance. We should include anomaly flags when they diverge.

sarah: On backward compatibility: we should expose a feature flag per tenant: legacy_matchmaker (bool). Migration plan: 1) shadow evaluate new contract for 2 weeks, 2) enable canary tenants, 3) flip for >95% traffic after no regressions.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for 3 tenants in prod: rdc-5, growth-2, internal-test. Logs -> https://internal/redwood/deploys/4302468012

kevin: Perf concerns: the unified contract includes a small expression runtime (subset of DSL). We should P95 test with 0, 10k, 100k qps to validate throughput. Aj, can infra run bench?

aj: I'll schedule bench jobs. quick note: expression runtime must be JIT-free on hot path. Prefer precompiled bytecode with bound inputs.

elana: Also need fallback semantics if the decider fails: matchmaker must have a safe degrade: prefer region affinity, then cost tier fallback, then broadhedge. Documented and tested.

sarah: For telemetry: add decision_id and route_fingerprint to every request. That way ops can tie matchmaker shadow to decider final.

kevin: Action items: 
- aj: bench evals + perf report (due EOD Thu)
- elana: draft migration playbook with feature-flag steps + rollback criteria (due Mon)
- sarah: telemetry schema PR (include fields: decision_id, preflight_hash, final_hash, divergence_reason)
- infra-bot: keep canary deployed and post status

elana: One more: policy language compatibility. We should support a compatibility shim that maps legacy predicates to the new subset, with warnings. No automatic semantic changes.

aj: ack. I'll add perf guardrails: max eval time per request, and circuit-breaker to stop evaluating expensive rules on high tail.

sarah: 👏 also let's add a short postmortem checklist to run after canary: latency regression, diversion rate, incorrect fallback rate, and cost delta.

kevin: Nice. If no objections I'll merge the migration doc into the RFC follow-up and start the feature flag flips after benches.

elana: No objections from me. :thumbsup:

aj: LGTM

sarah: LGTM

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary metrics: 3 tenants, 12h live, no error spikes, latency +1.2% p95. See dashboard -> https://internal/redwood/dashboards/decider-canary-4302468012

kevin: Great — thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after aj's perf report.
